FILRODENSWMB.UI.ReliefEmphasisHint: How strongly the light picks out land that rises gently over large areas, such as wide plains and long inland slopes. The terrain's heights don't change, only how it is lit.

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintReferenceResize: Shift+Scroll to resize the reference image

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintCropMove: Drag inside the crop area to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintCropResize: Drag a corner of the crop area to resize it

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveSpring: Drag a river source to move it

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDeletePoint: Ctrl+Click a point to delete it

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionPaint: Drag to paint land into the region

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionFill: Click to fill the outlined land with the region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRegionFillShift: Shift+Click a region to empty it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectRoute: Click a route to pick it and open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectFeature: Click a river or fault to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectMask: Click a land mask to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintSelectDecoration: Click a decoration to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditRoute: Double-click a route to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteFinish: Right-click, Enter or double-click to finish the route
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteUndoWaypoint: Backspace or Ctrl+Z to take the last click or stroke back
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteMoveWaypoint: Drag a waypoint to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteInsertWaypoint: Shift+Click the route to add a waypoint there
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteRemoveWaypoint: Ctrl+Click a waypoint to remove it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteSplit: Alt+Click a waypoint to split the route there
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteJoin: Alt+Drop an end waypoint on another route's end to join them
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRouteTrace: Drag to trace a stretch of the route

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveMask: Shift+Drag a point to move the whole land mask
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditMask: Double-click a point to edit the land mask

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMovePin: Drag a pin to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintResizePin: Hold a pin and Shift+Scroll to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDeletePin: Ctrl+Click a pin to delete it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditPin: Double-click a pin to open it in the inspector

FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveLabel: Drag a label to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRotateLabel: Hold a label and scroll to rotate it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintResizeLabel: Hold a label and Shift+Scroll to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditLabel: Double-click a label to open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintMoveDecoration: Drag a decoration or the scale bar to move it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintRotateDecoration: Hold a decoration and scroll to rotate it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintResizeDecoration: Hold a decoration and Shift+Scroll to resize it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintEditDecoration: Double-click a decoration to edit it
FILRODENSWMB.UI.HintDropMask: Release to drop the land mask
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutEscape: Escape to close a menu or dialogue
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutRegionLetGo: Escape to let go of the active region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutRegionStopStroke: Escape to end a stroke, or to let go of the active region
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShortcutRouteLetGo: Escape to let go of the route being edited
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonScene: New map sets where land is; Terrain sets how it looks.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonTerrain: Biomes read the terrain: settle sea level and relief first.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonBiomes: Rivers follow the terrain and the moisture the biomes read.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonFeatures: Regions divide the land the earlier tools have shaped.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonRegions: Regions, routes and pins, and labels can be worked in any order.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonInfrastructure: Every pin, route and region label is listed there too.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonLabels: Cartography adds the scale bar, border, grid and decorations.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextReasonCartography: Export saves the map as an image or a Foundry scene.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LatitudeHint: The latitudes of the map's top and bottom edges. They shape the climate, and so the biomes, and set the map's height in km.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapCropHint: Choose Crop on the bar and drag on the map to mark the area.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoCustomBiomes: No custom biomes yet. Add one with + in this section's title.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LabelLineWidthHint: Longest line, in characters, before the label wraps; 0 for no limit.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SaveStyleAsHint: Make a style from these fields, and use it here
FILRODENSWMB.UI.InspectorApplyHint: Changes apply at once; each is one undo step.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LabelFontsMissing: This map's labels use fonts this host lacks ({fonts}). They are drawn in {fallback} here, and keep their own font for a host that has it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportPngHint: Saves the map as a PNG image, showing the layers the map controls have switched on. The reference image is left out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSceneHint: Creates a Foundry scene from the map, with its grid. The next step asks for the scene's name and folder, and whether to add journal entries.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ScaleTooltip: Lower values result in larger, more continuous continents.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.StretchTooltip: Higher values flatten valleys into continental shelves and push peaks higher.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MapTransformHint: Nudge the camera to explore adjacent landmasses, or zoom out to generate larger, sweeping continents.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RiverMeanderHint: How much rivers meander where the land is flat. At 0 they never meander; above 1 they also meander on gentler slopes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RiverWidthHint: Scales how wide every river is drawn. Rivers still start narrow and widen as tributaries join them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AreaFactorHint: How much smaller the world is than its latitudes alone would make it. The map's latitudes set its height in km; the area factor divides the world's area by this number, so a continent spanning most of the map has the size of a believable medieval realm rather than a whole Earth. It sets what a pixel measures in km for the distances the module works out from the map's scale (how far settlements and routes are apart when they are generated, say) and changes nothing that is drawn. 15 is the default; 1 is a true-to-latitude world.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSettingsHint: Bundle your custom biomes and quick styles into a shareable file.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportSettingsNoneSelect: Select at least one category to export.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsHint: Load custom biomes and quick styles shared by another GM.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsSuccessWit: Imported {count} item(s) into this map ({duplicates} already present, skipped).
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsAllDuplica: Every item in that file is already in this map's Style Library. Nothing new to import.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsEmpty: That file didn't contain any recognized custom biomes or quick styles.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ImportSettingsError: Failed to import settings. Please check the file and try again.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ReliefShadingHint: Shades slopes as if lit from the north-west, so hills, valleys and seabed features stand out, with or without biomes. Set to 0 to turn off.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SeabedReliefHint: How much of the relief shading still shows through deep water. At 0 the sea floor's shape fades with depth; at 1 its ridges and trenches stay as sharp as on land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WaterHueHint: The hue of the sea and lakes, from blue-green through blue to blue-violet. Depth still decides how light or dark the water is.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WaterClarityHint: How deep you can see into the water. Higher values show more of the seabed and its biomes further from the shore.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoCustomStyles: No styles yet. Make one with Save as… in an inspector, or with + in this section's title.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.QuickStyleUsageTooltip: Used by {count} feature(s) on this map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MassEditHint: Tick a field to apply it to every selected item. Fields left unticked keep each item's current value.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BuiltinPinIconsHint: Hide icons you don't use to keep the picker tidy. The default pin icon can't be hidden.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinIconProtected: This is the default pin icon and can't be hidden
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoCustomPinIcons: No custom pin icons yet. Add one with + in this section's title.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinIconWhiteCheckHint: Custom pin icons must be solid white on a transparent background to render correctly - check the preview above before accepting.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemovePinIconConfirm: Remove the custom icon "{name}"? This only removes it from the picker - the SVG file itself won't be touched.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RemovePinIconInUseWarnin: "{name}" is currently used by {count} pin(s). Removing it will change those pins to the default icon. This only removes the icon from the picker - the SVG file itself won't be touched. Continue?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UnresolvedPinIconsWarnin: {count} pin(s) on this map use custom icons not registered in this world, and are showing the default icon instead.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FlatTextureHint: Gives the new Flat map a fine, natural texture instead of perfectly flat ground. Smooth removes it and Roughen puts it back. Applies when you select Create New Map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ResolutionWarningContent: Changing the map resolution alters the underlying pixel grid. This will wipe all custom terrain painting, biome painting, and hand-placed springs. Are you sure you wish to proceed?
FILRODENSWMB.Web.StorageUnavailable: This browser is not letting the map builder store anything, so saved maps will be lost when the page closes. Export maps you want to keep.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GridDataSizeMismatch: The exported scene's grid is not the size its grid data was worked out for, so the grid data will not match the scene's grid cells. See the console for details.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SaveError: Failed to save the map. Please ensure the compendium is unlocked.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SelectMap: Select a saved map from the compendium:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PreparingMapMigrate: Preparing map: migrating regions and routes...
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MapUpgraded: This map's regions and routes have been converted to the new format. Save the map to keep the conversion.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MeshRebuilt: This map's mesh no longer matched the map and has been rebuilt. Check its regions and routes, then save the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MeshOwnersLost: Some regions could not be restored and are now empty: {detail}
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MeshLoadFailed: This map's regions and routes could not be prepared. They are kept as they were saved and are not shown.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionStyleFillOnlyHint: A region quick style sets a region's fill. Its border comes from its level's line style.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModeSelect: Select: click a region to paint it and open it in the inspector
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModePaint: Paint land into the region (Shift: erase)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModeErase: Erase any region under the brush (Shift: paint)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionModeFill: Fill: click to give the region the connected land shown (Shift: empty a region)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShowAllLevelsHint: While painting, only the level being painted and the levels above it are drawn. Turn this on to draw every level and set as the map shows them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnNoActiveRegion: Choose a region to paint (click one on the map or in the Regions panel), or add a new one.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnOutsideParent: Start painting inside a region of the parent level: this level's regions stay inside their parent regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ChildCellsCleared: {count} cells of the levels below are now unassigned, since the ground above them changed region. Auto-Assign Cells in a level's menu can fill them again.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteLevelConfirm: Delete the level {name}? Its {regions} regions and {cells} painted cells go with it, and the {childLevels} levels below it move up to its parent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LayerSetsHint: A new layer set: one way of dividing the map (for example Political or Climate), shown over the map on its own.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteLayerSetConfirm: Delete the layer set {name}? Its {levels} levels and {regions} regions go with it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LayerSetOpacityHint: Multiplies the fill opacity of every level in the set, so the whole set can be faded without changing the balance between its levels.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LayerSetWaterTintHint: Shows a faint fill where the set's regions claim water. Off, regions are filled over land only.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NestingFreeHint: Free nesting: this level's regions may cross the borders of its parent level's regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NestingProblemsHint: {count} cells lie outside their region's parent region. Fix Nesting in the level's menu repairs them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AddLayerHint: A new layer below, named by its tier until you rename it. Its regions sit inside the regions of the layer above.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ChooseParentRegion: Choose a region in {name} to see its regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UnassignedHint: Regions without a single parent region (free nesting, or painted before parents were kept).
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NameNewSet: Name of the new layer set
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AutoAssignHint: Gives the unassigned land inside each parent region to the nearest of this level's regions in that parent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.AutoAssigned: {count} cells assigned to the regions of {name}.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FixNestingHint: Gives each region the parent region holding most of its cells, and unassigns its cells outside that parent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelTitleTemplateHint: How a region's title reads at this level, with {name} standing for the region's name (for example "Kingdom of {name}").
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelNestingHint: Constrained: a region is painted only inside its parent region, and painting a parent region clears the child cells it takes. Free: regions may cross their parent's borders.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelWatersHint: How far this level's regions claim the sea from their coasts, in map pixels (the scale bar in the Cartography tool can show what a pixel is in your map's units). Water goes to the nearest region, so neighbours meet halfway; a lake with one region on all its shores is wholly that region's. At 0 regions own land only. The waters follow every stroke.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LevelScaleWithMapHint: Off, border thicknesses are map pixels. On, they grow and shrink with the map's resolution, as pins and labels do.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnNoLevel: Add a level before adding regions.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionsHint: A new region in this list, ready to paint. Clicking unclaimed land while painting also makes one.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MergeRegionHint: The cells of {name} join the region chosen below, and {name} is removed.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.MergeNoOther: This level has no other region to merge into.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LoadWarningContent: Loading a map will overwrite your current canvas. Any unsaved brush strokes or pins will be lost. Are you sure you wish to proceed?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoSavedMaps: No saved maps found in the compendium.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoPoints: No pins yet. Choose Place on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoRoutes: No routes yet. Choose Route and Draw on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.Name: Name
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinStyleHint: A named look for a kind of place: its icon, colour and size, and its label's size and visibility. A pin made with a style follows the style when it is edited. Pin styles are managed in the Style Library.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinStyleLabelHint: What the label of a pin made with this style starts with. A label quick style sets its font, colour, width and alignment; the size here is used over the quick style's own.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PinDetailLevelHint: How prominent the places with this style are. Level 0 places are always shown; higher levels are the first to be hidden when a map is viewed at world scale. It does not change how a pin is drawn.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextRouteStyleHint: The style the next route drawn gets. A route's own look is changed in its inspector.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NextLabelStyleHint: The style the next label placed gets. A label's text and look are changed in its inspector.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteLegModeHint: How the legs between waypoints are found. Follow Terrain finds the easiest way for the transport, avoiding steep ground and keeping to the ground it can use. Straight joins the waypoints directly.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteTransportHint: What travels the route, chosen when it is drawn. Roads keep to land and prefer to join existing roads; sea routes keep to water.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteTransportFixedHint: Chosen when the route was drawn. A road's waypoints are all on land and a sea route's all on water, so a finished route cannot change transport.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteSpanWaterHint: Lets a Follow Terrain road cross water between its waypoints, as a bridge, causeway or ferry, at a steep cost per cell of water: it bridges a strait when going round would be longer and keeps to land otherwise. It can only bridge water about twelve cells wide; wider water needs a sea route. Its waypoints must still be on land. Applies to legs found from now on; Re-path in the editor applies it to a finished route.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteDetailHint: How closely a traced stroke is kept, in map cells. A bend becomes a waypoint when the stroke strays further than this from the line between the bends either side of it, and a long run without a bend gains waypoints along it so the route keeps near the stroke. 1 keeps every bend; higher values keep fewer waypoints and leave more to the path finding.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteDetailEditorHint: Used by Simplify: a waypoint is dropped when it lies within this many map cells of the line between its neighbours. The same setting as the toolbar's Detail.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteClassHint: The route's importance, for other modules and the exported data. It does not change how the route is drawn.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteOutlineHint: Draws a thin dark edge along both sides of the line, so it stands out from the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RouteSmoothingHint: Rounds the corners of the line where it turns from cell to cell.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnRouteUnreachable: That waypoint cannot be reached from the last one: a road keeps to land (bridging only narrow water when Span Water is on) and a sea route to water.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.WarnRouteStrokeSkipped: {count} bends of the stroke could not be reached (off the route's ground, or across water it cannot bridge) and were left out.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LabelHelpText: Click to add a new label. Drag labels to reposition them. Use the scroll wheel while dragging to rotate them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoLabels: No labels yet. Choose Place on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoDecorations: No decorations yet. Add one with Add decoration.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SeedWarningContent: Generating a new terrain seed will permanently erase all manual brush edits you have applied to this map. Do you want to continue?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UnsavedChangesWarning: You have unsaved changes. Do you want to save your map before closing?
FILRODENSWMB.JOURNAL.Title: World Map Parameter Log
FILRODENSWMB.JOURNAL.Description: This journal contains the full generation profile and mathematical vectors used during world creation. This allows you to see the complete settings for the model without having to load it.
FILRODENSWMB.JOURNAL.StandardPalette: No custom biome colors applied. Standard palette active.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SceneNameHint: The name of the new Scene that will be created in your world.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ExportFolderHint: The folder inside your world directory where the map images will be saved.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.GenerateJournalsHint: Automatically creates a Journal Entry for this map and populates it with your Points of Interest, linking them natively to the Scene.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CreateGMOverlayHint: Generates a transparent secondary tile containing hidden routes and labels, invisible to players by default.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OverwriteJournalsHint: If checked, existing map journals will be updated with your current descriptions. Warning: This will destroy any manual lore edits made by the GM.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ThemeModeHint: Light or dark. Automatic follows Foundry's interface theme, or in the web version your system's setting.
FILRODENSWMB.Settings.ThemeHue.Name: Color Theme
FILRODENSWMB.Settings.ThemeHue.Hint: Select the primary hue for the interface.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteBiomeConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this custom biome? Any existing areas on the map will return to their original biomes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BiomeCodeHint: Optional, e.g. a system's terrain code
FILRODENSWMB.UI.BiomePlacementHint: Where this biome can appear. Painting and auto-generation rules only place it there, and it is never shown anywhere else. Underwater biomes lie on the bed of the sea or a lake, seen through the water. Overwater biomes sit on top of the water, such as pack ice.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PreviewFallbackCoverageH: Preview Rule Coverage: hover to highlight every area currently using a default biome rather than one of your custom rules.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorIntro: Rules run top to bottom - the first range a pixel's elevation, moisture, and temperature all fall inside wins. Defaults sit permanently at the bottom as a guaranteed fallback and can't be reordered or edited.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorLegendOverlap: Ranges on the same axis are allowed to overlap.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorLegendSeaLevel: Dashed line on Elevation = sea level, shown for reference - custom ranges can cross it freely, including to define water biomes.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorNoRulesYet: No auto-generation rules yet - this biome will only appear where it's hand-painted.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorDefaultsHint: Read-only - shown for reference so new rules can fit around or combine these.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorSeaLevelToolti: Sea level (reference only - ranges aren't restricted by it)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RuleEditorAddIndependent: Adds another, separate rule for this biome - matched independently of the rows above it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EditCanvas: Create Regional Map from Existing Map
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EditCanvasHint: Creates a regional map based on a crop of the existing map, preserving all edits. This provides enhanced detail in the terrain and biome layers.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoFaultLines: No fault lines yet. Choose Fault on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultStyleHint: Simple raises and enlarges the land's own hills and valleys. Fold Belt lays long parallel ridges along the range. Rugged cuts sharp ridges and valleys running down from the crest.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultThicknessHint: How far the feature spreads from its line, in pixels. For a mountain range, rift or subduction zone this is its width either side of the line; for a hotspot chain it is the width of the band its islands lie in, and a young island is about a third of it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultStrengthHint: How pronounced the feature is: the height of a mountain range or of a subduction zone's volcanic arc, the depth of a rift, or the height of a hotspot chain's youngest volcanoes above sea level.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultArcDistanceHint: How far from the trench the chain of volcanoes rises, as a share of the width. The volcanoes stand on the left side of the direction the line was drawn in.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultTrenchDepthHint: How deep the trench along the line cuts into the seabed.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultFloorTextureHint: How rough the rift floor is: 0 leaves smooth sediment, 1 adds young lava fields and small fault blocks.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultVolcanoesHint: How many volcanoes rise on the rift floor and its shoulders. Set to 0 for none.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultSpacingHint: The typical distance between volcanoes, in island sizes. Low values merge neighboring volcanoes into larger islands.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultSpacingTrendHint: Negative values crowd the volcanoes closer together towards the young end of the chain; positive values spread them further apart, as if the plate sped up.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultScatterHint: How far volcanoes stray either side of the line.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultVariationHint: How much island sizes and the gaps between them vary. At 0 every island is the typical size and evenly spaced.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultPulsesHint: How much the hotspot's output rises and falls along the chain. High values give clusters of large islands separated by long empty stretches.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultVentsHint: How often extra volcanoes grow on an island's flanks, merging into one larger island.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultDrownedHint: The share of the chain, from its oldest end, that has sunk below the sea as atolls and seamounts.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.FaultReverseHint: When ticked, the feature runs from the last point drawn to the first: a subduction zone's volcanoes rise on the right side of the line as drawn instead of the left side, and a hotspot chain's youngest volcano is at its first point instead of its last.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoManualRivers: No rivers drawn yet. Choose River on the bar, then click the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PromoteConfirm: Clone this regional map to a standalone master map?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.PauseTerrainGeneration: Pause automatic Terrain Generation (use the Apply button to manually regenerate the terrain)
FILRODENSWMB.UI.LandMaskHint: Draw polygons: Select '+' to add land and '-' to add ocean.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EditLandMaskHint: Mark areas of the map that could be land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DrawLandMaskHint: Draw areas of the map that could be land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DrawOceanMaskHint: Draw areas of the map that could be ocean.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RandomLandMaskHint: Add a random shape of the selected type. Remove Land shapes are always placed over existing land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RandomLandMaskNoLand: There is no land on the map for a random Remove Land shape to cut into.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RandomLandMapHint: Add a random map of land and sea: landmasses as Add Land shapes, with Remove Land shapes for the lakes and seas inside them.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.NoLandMasks: No land masks yet. Choose Land or Ocean on the bar, then draw on the map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteAllLandMasksHint: Delete every land mask drawn on this map.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.DeleteAllLandMasksConfir: Are you sure you want to delete all {count} land masks from this map?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineStandardHint: Uses standard noise generation to create quick, randomized terrain.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineFlatHint: Creates a completely flat landmass at sea level, acting as a blank canvas for manual terrain brushing.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineAdvancedHint: Simulates tectonic plate collisions to build realistic continents, deep trenches, and mountain ridges.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.EngineGuidedHint: Uses your hand-drawn vector masks to dictate exact landmass and ocean placements.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TectonicPlatesHintV2: Controls the number of tectonic plates. Each plate is either buoyant continental crust or sinking ocean floor, so the plates decide where the continents lie. Where plates collide they raise mountain ranges on land and trenches at sea; where they pull apart they open rift valleys on land and mid-ocean ridges at sea.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OceanRidgesHintTectonic: How high the mid-ocean ridges rise from the deep ocean floor. Ridges form where tectonic plates pull apart under the ocean, and fade out towards the continental slopes. Set to 0 for a flat ocean floor.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TectonicPlatesHint: Controls the number of shifting plates. Higher values create more frequent mountain ridges and fault-line valleys across the landmass, but will not significantly alter the global coastline.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CoastlineFractureHint: Bends and distorts the edges of the continents. Higher values create undulating bays and  peninsulas, while lower values keep landmasses rounder and smoother.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ContinentalGroupingHint: Adjusts the baseline grouping of land. Higher values flood the map; lower values merge landmasses together.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.SurfaceRoughnessHint: Adds high-frequency detail. Low values create rolling hills; high values create jagged, rocky peaks.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ErosionScaleHint: Zooms the detail noise. Lower values cluster mountains tightly; higher values stretch features across broader areas.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ContinentScaleHint: How far inland the land takes to reach its full height, beyond the Coastal Plains. Lower values create steep coastal mountains; higher values create broad, gradual slopes. Islands smaller than this rise over their own size instead, so they still have hills. Measured in pixels of a 1000 pixel map and scaled to your map's size, so the same value looks the same at any resolution.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OceanRidgesHint: How high the mid-ocean ridges rise from the deep ocean floor. Ridges run down the middle of the ocean between continents, where the seabed is equally far from both, and fade out towards the continental slopes. Small islands do not create ridges. Set to 0 for a flat ocean floor.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.OceanScaleHint: How far out the seabed takes to fall to the deep ocean floor, beyond the Continental Shelf. Lower values create abrupt drops into deep water; higher values create broad, gradual slopes and shallower seas between nearby coasts. Measured in pixels of a 1000 pixel map and scaled to your map's size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ContinentScaleHintLegacy: Defines the gradient slope. Lower values create steep coastal mountains; higher values create sprawling, flat coastal plains.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShelfRangeHint: Controls the width of the shallow water transition zone before dropping into deep ocean.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.ShelfWidthHint: Width of the band of shallow sea along the coast, beyond which the seabed falls steeply to the deep ocean floor. Set to 0 for coasts that drop straight into deep water. Each 0.1 is 10 pixels on a 1000 pixel map, scaled to your map's size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.CoastalPlainsHint: Width of the band of low, gently rolling land along the coast before the land starts to rise. Set to 0 to let the terrain rise straight from the shore. Each 0.1 is 10 pixels on a 1000 pixel map, scaled to your map's size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntro: This regional map was created with older terrain rules. Updating it makes it match its parent map more closely:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateTerrain: Finer terrain detail, such as more intricate coastlines. The overall shape of the land stays the same.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateFaults: Fault lines and hotspot chains at the same size as on the parent map. They were narrower than on the parent, with their texture and volcanoes drawn at a different scale; they are widened to their width on the parent and drawn at its scale.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateBiomes: Biomes that match the parent map. Rain shadows were placed too far downwind, so some forests, grasslands and deserts will move. Biome borders also gain finer detail.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateNotSaved: The update is not saved automatically. Reloading the map without saving returns it to how it was. Saving the map keeps the update.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateDismiss: Don't ask again for this map
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateDismissHint: You can still update this map later with the update button at the top of the Create New Map tool.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateApplied: Map updated. Save the map to keep the update, or reload it to return to the original.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.UpdateMapHint: This map was created with older terrain rules. Update it to use the latest terrain engine.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroTecton: This map was created with the original tectonic engine (Advanced (Tectonics) v1). Updating it to Advanced (Tectonics) v2 builds the map's terrain with a new engine, so it will look completely different:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateTectonicsLa: The continents, coastlines, mountain ranges and oceans are built afresh from the same seed and settings. Nothing of the current layout is kept: land may become sea and sea may become land.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateTectonicsFe: Everything placed on the map (pins, routes, regions, labels, rivers and terrain brush strokes) stays exactly where it is, so it may no longer fit the new land. Only update a map you are happy to rework.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroCoastl: This map was created with older terrain rules. Updating it to the latest guided terrain engine changes it as follows:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateFracture: Coastal Fracture is lowered from {before} to {after}, which keeps your coastline close to its current shape. From now on, the same value gives the same look on a map of any size.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateCoastlines: Coastal Fracture and Continent Scale used to be fixed sizes in pixels, so they had less effect the larger the map. They are now scaled to the map's size, so the same values look the same at any resolution, and coastlines gain finer detail.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateProfile: Oceans become deeper. Continental Shelf now sets the width of a band of shallow sea along the coast, beyond which the seabed falls steeply to the deep ocean floor. The new Coastal Plains setting adds a band of low land along the coast. Continent Scale now only sets how steeply the land rises, and the new Ocean Scale (starting at your current Continent Scale) sets how steeply the sea deepens. Small islands now rise to proper hills, and mid-ocean ridges rise between continents (see the new Mid-Ocean Ridges setting). The land masks you drew stay the same.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroFaults: This map was created with older terrain rules. Updating it changes its fault lines as follows:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateFeatures: Fault lines become the new tectonic features: convergent faults become mountain ranges, divergent faults become rifts, and hotspot chains become the new hotspot chains, running from their oldest volcano to their youngest. They look different, and you can adjust them afterwards.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateSlip: Slip faults are removed, since the new tectonic features have no equivalent.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateIntroRivers: This map was created with older river rules. Updating it changes its rivers as follows:
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateRivers: Rivers follow the lie of the land more closely instead of running in straight lines, a river that runs beside another joins it, and a lake that fills up breaks out through its lowest shore so its river flows on. River sources are placed afresh from the land and climate (the ones you added yourself are kept), so many rivers take a different course, and some lakes move, grow or shrink.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.TerrainUpdateChannels: Custom rivers run exactly along the line you drew, carry on downhill from its end, and are drawn like any other river. The ground around each is lowered into a gentle valley that keeps the texture of the land, in place of the old channel.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapNeedsUpdate: This map was created with older terrain rules. Update it to the latest engine (see the Create New Map tool) to create regional maps from it.
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapSaveFirstNew: This map has not been saved yet. A regional map is listed under the map it was created from, so save this map first. Save it now and create the regional map?
FILRODENSWMB.UI.RegionalMapSaveFirstChan: This map has unsaved changes. A regional map is created from the map as you see it, so save the changes first to keep the saved map and its regional map matching. Save now and create the regional map?
